title: Extract-N-Amp Equivalent DNA Extraction Protocol
author: Stephen D Douglas Russell
materials: DNA grade 1 M Tris buffer pH 8.0

Optional: Particularly for older specimens or recalcitrant tissue, add a 1.0mm stainless steel ball bearing to each tube, 50uL of low TE solution, and then vortex them for about 5 minutes. We have a BioSpec Mini-BeadBeater 96 and/or a Qiagen Tissue Lyser III for this purpose. The addition of low TE at this point allows the tissue to be properly disrupted. With only 20uL of ES, the tissue tends to get stuck on the sidewall of the tube and not consistently fragmented. Vortex the tubes for 00:00:05 and spin them down for 00:00:05 . We typically do this on a PCR rack and vortex 6 or 12 strips at a time, and spin down two plates at a time. Note: We typically do not bead-beat most modern specimens that pass through for extraction - adding 80uL of low TE after the upcoming 10 minute incubation step - just before the template is about to be utilized into the final PCR plates. Bead-beating is typically not needed for 99% of specimens/species of macrofungi. For older fungarium/museum collections, or collections over 5 years old, the bead-beating process in this step (13) is critical. Success rates will significantly diminish without it.

steps.title: Add molecular water
steps.instruction: In a flowhood, measure the appropriate volume of molecular‑grade water into a sterile 50 mL tube (e.g., 350 mL for 500 mL final product). For other batch sizes use 70 mL for 100 mL, 175 mL for 250 mL, 350 mL for 500 mL, or 700 mL for 1000 mL final volume.

steps.title: Add and dissolve KCl
steps.instruction: Add the corresponding amount of KCl to the water and swirl until fully dissolved (9.3 g for 500 mL final product; 1.86 g for 100 mL, 4.65 g for 250 mL, 18.6 g for 1000 mL).

steps.title: Add 0.5 M EDTA
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of 0.5 M EDTA (10 mL for 500 mL final product; 2 mL for 100 mL, 5 mL for 250 mL, 20 mL for 1000 mL).

steps.title: Add 1 M Tris buffer
steps.instruction: Add the correct volume of DNA‑grade 1 M Tris pH 8.0‑8.5 (50 mL for 500 mL final product; 10 mL for 100 mL, 25 mL for 250 mL, 100 mL for 1000 mL) to the mixture.

steps.title: Adjust pH with NaOH
steps.instruction: Add 1 M NaOH starting with 10 mL, then add 1 mL increments until the pH is above 9 (target 9‑9.5). For 500 mL final product the typical total is 13 mL; subsequent batches can use this fixed amount without re‑measuring.

steps.title: Bring to final volume
steps.instruction: Top up the solution with molecular‑grade water to reach the desired total volume (100 mL, 500 mL, or 1000 mL). Example: add 989.9 mL water to reach 1 L after all other components.

steps.title: Filter‑sterilize and store
steps.instruction: Filter‑sterilize the solution using a vacuum flask and a 0.22 µm filter (mandatory if prepared outside a laminar flow cabinet). Aliquot into sterile 50 mL tubes and store at 4 °C for up to 1 year (or keep extracts at –20 °C).

steps.title: Add 200 µL 0.5 M EDTA
steps.instruction: Using sterile, filtered tips, add 200 µL of 0.5 M EDTA to the solution that will be used for diluting raw DNA extracts.

steps.title: Place tissue in strip tube
steps.instruction: Put a small amount of tissue into one well of an 8‑strip tube and record the specimen identity in a spreadsheet.

steps.title: Add extraction solution
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of the prepared Extraction Solution to each tube (use 30 µL per tube for toothpick extractions).

steps.title: Incubate at 80 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes for 10 minutes at 80 °C, typically in a thermocycler.

steps.title: Add low TE (optional)
steps.instruction: For modern specimens, add 80 µL of low TE solution after incubation (40 µL for toothpick extractions). Skip this step if low TE was already added during a prior bead‑beating step.

steps.title: Use extract for PCR
steps.instruction: Use 0.5 µL of the final extract directly as template in a PCR reaction. Store remaining extract at –20 °C; DNA remains viable for years.
